title: Verdier-compatible open and closed recollement for arbitrary-field adic coefficients
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. For $W=X,Z,U$ use exactly $\mathcal C_W=D^b_c(W,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], its standard cohomology of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], and the relative dual $D_W$ of [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality]. Pullback and direct image mean the completed, rationalized common-stage operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image], and $j_!$ means the compact-support operation of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Define $i^!=D_Zi^*D_X$.

All six functors $j_!,j^*,Rj_*,i^*,Ri_*,i^!$ preserve these bounded constructible categories and are exact triangulated functors. There are adjunctions $j_!\dashv j^*\dashv Rj_*$ and $i^*\dashv Ri_*\dashv i^!$. The adjunction maps give isomorphisms
$$j^*j_!\cong\operatorname{id},\quad j^*Rj_*\cong\operatorname{id},\quad i^*Ri_*\cong\operatorname{id},\quad i^!Ri_*\cong\operatorname{id},$$
and $j^*Ri_*=0$, $i^*j_!=0$, $i^!Rj_*=0$. For every $K\in\mathcal C_X$ the adjunction maps occur in distinguished triangles
$$j_!j^*K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Ri_*i^*K\longrightarrow j_!j^*K[1],$$
$$Ri_*i^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow Ri_*i^!K[1].$$
There are natural isomorphisms $j^*D_X\cong D_Uj^*$ and $i^*D_X\cong D_Zi^!$, compatible with shifts and finite coefficient extension. The functors $i^*,j^*$ commute with standard cohomology, and their geometric fibres are the restricted geometric fibres.

source.place: Lemmas 6.7.2, 6.7.7, 6.7.19 and 6.7.20, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; recollement identities and dual restriction formulated for the exact common-stage categories, as an agent formulation of these operations.
